challenges.title: Build your own std::vector
challenges.tagline: Eight stages from an empty class to a standard-conforming dynamic array, with exception safety and move semantics tested along the way.

challenges.title: Build your own chess engine
challenges.tagline: Nine stages from bitboards, directional shifts, and magic bitboards to Perft-verified legal movegen, alpha-beta with quiescence, transposition tables, and UCI.

challenges.title: Build your own allocator
challenges.tagline: Write a minimal allocator, then an arena and a pool, and plug them into containers.
challenges.note: Allocator-aware containers, std::pmr and arena or pool resources are easiest to understand once you have written the raw-storage and relocation code of a vector yourself.

challenges.title: Build your own task and generator
challenges.tagline: Implement promise types, awaiters and symmetric transfer by writing a lazy task and a generator from scratch.
challenges.note: Starts from the coroutine frame and promise_type machinery, with no prerequisite challenge.

challenges.title: Build your own std::execution
challenges.tagline: Build senders, receivers and operation states, then compose them into algorithms such as then and when_all.
challenges.note: Senders and receivers are awaitable and coroutine tasks are senders, so writing your own task and awaiters first makes the connect/start model and operation-state lifetimes much clearer.
